decision: Bind REAL-WORKER readiness to fresh qrexec campaign provenance and the exact tested commit.
selectedApproach: campaign_start/campaign_end framing carried through collector into readiness gate

reviewers.assessment: Counters and latency alone are insufficient because a clean synthetic or stale report can satisfy the gate. Provenance must be part of the evaluated artifact.
Require qrexec transport, distinct source/target Qubes, service identity, run identity, timestamps, and exact git SHA. Fail closed when any evidence is absent.
Event framing adds constant-size metadata only at campaign boundaries, avoiding per-request cryptographic or database overhead and preserving transport latency measurements.

alternatives.name: trust numeric collector output only
alternatives.rejectedBecause: cannot distinguish real Qubes execution from simulation, stale output, or a different commit

alternatives.name: per-event signed attestation
alternatives.rejectedBecause: requires key lifecycle and trusted signer placement before the first real Qubes campaign is proven

alternatives.name: campaign boundary provenance plus freshness and git binding

required: distinct source and target Qube names
single matching campaign start/end run ID
40-hex commit SHA matching the expected tested head
existing correctness counters and latency budgets
qa.currentEvidence: Source and regression tests added; GitHub Actions result still inaccessible to the current integration and must not be inferred.

failuresAndLessons: A readiness gate that validates only outcome metrics can accidentally bless simulation evidence.
Provenance should be generated at the harness boundary and preserved by the collector rather than manually appended later.
Commit binding prevents a successful campaign for older code from certifying newer untested code.
Cryptographic dom0-backed attestation remains a later hardening option after real qrexec execution is available.
